# "The Ramp": reference footage

`the-ramp.mp4` is Tesla's official clip "The Ramp | Roadster" (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7p5LxFdc-Qg, 1920x1080, 23.976 fps, 45.6 s), filmed at night at the SpaceX rocket test site in McGregor, Texas, during the Roadster reveal on October 15-16, 2026. Tesla describes it as "the first live demo during the Roadster event".

The JPEG files are stills from that clip, in story order. Times are clip time in seconds.

## What happens

The same stunt is shown from several angles:

| Clip time | Event |
|---|---|
| 0-1 s | Behind the car, which is stopped at the foot of the ramp. |
| 2-7 s | Wide side shot: the car drives up the curve, through vertical, toward the lip. |
| 7-9.5 s | The car sits near the lip, past vertical and upside down, held to the surface by fan downforce. |
| 9.5-10.5 s | It leaves the lip belly-up and falls away from the ramp. Attitude jets fire and roll it back toward wheels-down. |
| 10.5-11.5 s | Downward jets brake the fall. Touchdown on four wheels at the foot of the ramp. |
| 11.5-16 s | A large white smoke cloud spreads out. The car drives out of the smoke and away. |
| 17-25 s | Closer angle of the lip, the release, the roll, the low hover on downward jets, and the touchdown. |
| 27-30 s | Drone shot looking down past the lip at the rolling car and its jets. |
| 31-45 s | High aerial: the hook profile of the ramp and its truss tower, and cars on the lit approach. |

## Frames

| File | Time | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| `01-rear-at-ramp-foot.jpg` | 0.5 | Car from behind at the foot of the ramp. Concrete-grey running surface with stains, a white centre line, red LED strips on both edges, the truss frame on the right. Full-width red tail light bar, `RDSTR` plate, round nozzles in the dark rear diffuser. |
| `02-wide-ramp-start.jpg` | 2.5 | Wide side shot: the ramp alone in the dark, rising from flat into a tall hook. Red strip lights on the ground. |
| `03-wide-climb-curve.jpg` | 4.0 | Car on the lower curve. |
| `04-wide-climb-vertical.jpg` | 5.5 | Car on the vertical section. |
| `05-wide-near-lip.jpg` | 6.5 | Car nearly at the lip. |
| `06-wide-hanging-inverted.jpg` | 8.0 | Car near the lip, past vertical, upside down. |
| `07-wide-leaving-lip.jpg` | 9.5 | The car has left the lip. |
| `08-wide-falling-inverted.jpg` | 10.0 | Falling beside the ramp, still belly-up. |
| `09-wide-jets-rolling.jpg` | 10.5 | Jets firing as the car rolls upright. |
| `10-wide-jets-braking.jpg` | 11.0 | Low above the ground, wheels down, downward jets braking the fall. |
| `11-wide-touchdown.jpg` | 11.5 | Touchdown, smoke starting to burst outward. |
| `12-wide-smoke-cloud.jpg` | 12.5 | Wide white smoke cloud at the foot of the ramp. |
| `13-wide-driving-out-of-smoke.jpg` | 14.0 | The car drives out of the cloud, headlights on. |

| `19-close-touchdown.jpg` | 22.5 | Touchdown at the foot of the ramp, smoke bursting out. |
| `20-close-smoke-cloud.jpg` | 24.0 | The cloud expanding beside the ramp. |
| `21-drone-top-down-roll.jpg` | 27.5 | Drone above the lip looking down: the car rolling in the air with three jets, the ramp's red edge lights below. |

---
name: dev-browser
description: Browser automation with persistent page state using the dev-browser CLI. Use when the user mentions browse, open website, click, fill form, screenshot, scrape, automate browser, test website, log into, navigate, web page, or any browser interaction.
allowed-tools:
  - Bash(dev-browser *)
  - Bash(chrome-dev *)
  - Bash(/Applications/Helium.app/Contents/MacOS/Helium *)
---

Drive every browser task with the `dev-browser` CLI.

## Default: Chrome Dev (one shared, signed-in Chrome)

Always run against **Chrome Dev**, Melvyn's single persistent Chrome (profile `~/.chrome-dev-profile`, CDP port 9333) where he is signed in to his accounts:

```bash
chrome-dev start   # idempotent: launches it if needed, prints http://127.0.0.1:9333
dev-browser --connect http://127.0.0.1:9333 <<'EOF'
const page = await browser.getPage("main");
EOF
```

- Need a clean logged-out session? Use `--headless`, or `DEV_BROWSER_ISOLATED=1 dev-browser --browser <name>`, and say so.
- Use descriptive page names per task (`browser.getPage("lumail-checkout")`) so parallel agents do not fight over the same tab. Close pages you no longer need with `browser.closePage(name)`. Never close Melvyn's own tabs.
- If a site asks for login in Chrome Dev, stop and ask Melvyn to sign in there (it persists). Never type passwords.
- Enforced: `dev-browser` is a shim (`~/cc/scripts/chrome-dev/dev-browser-wrapper`) that auto-starts Chrome Dev and adds `--connect http://127.0.0.1:9333` to every run, even with `--browser <name>`. It passes through untouched only with `--connect <url>`, `--headless`, or `DEV_BROWSER_ISOLATED=1` (headed throwaway Chromium, e.g. WebGL capture or HTML-to-image rendering that must not pop tabs in Chrome Dev). Never launch Chrome for Testing for normal browsing.
- `chrome-dev status|stop` to inspect or quit it. Melvyn can also open it from Spotlight: "Chrome Dev".

Never use Cursor IDE Browser MCP (`cursor-ide-browser`, `browser_navigate`, `browser_snapshot`, `browser_lock`, `browser_click`, `browser_cdp`, or any `browser_*` tool).

If `dev-browser` is missing: obey the repo's package-manager rules (no `npm install -g` when npm is forbidden). In Codex, prefer the bundled Node/Playwright/Chromium runtime for page-load, screenshot, console, and interaction checks. Install the CLI only when npm is allowed and the task needs persistence or CDP the bundled runtime cannot provide: `npm install -g dev-browser && dev-browser install`. When falling back to Playwright, keep the same proof (URL, title, errors, screenshots, exact steps) and state that the CLI was unavailable.

Write one-thing scripts. Reuse named pages (`browser.getPage("main")`) across runs. End each script by logging JSON state. Commands, flags, Page methods, locators, screenshots, forms, and CDP connect: [api-reference.md](references/api-reference.md). Open that file before inventing a Page method.

File I/O is only `~/.dev-browser/tmp/`. Never pass absolute paths to `saveScreenshot` or `writeFile`; copy out from the returned tmp path.

Helium is not auto-discovered. Launch it with `--remote-debugging-port` and connect with `dev-browser --browser helium --connect http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. An already-running Helium without CDP cannot be attached; if it must not restart, use AppleScript or Computer Use.

On script failure, the page stays put. Reconnect, screenshot, log URL/title, then continue.

</skill-body>
</read-skill-result>

event.text:
Done — the stunt completes cleanly in the default run, and every failure mode crashes differently under the same physics.

Open [index.html](/tmp/workspace.oOeyMl/app/index.html) in a browser. It is a single self-contained file (1,435 lines); Three.js r160 loads from a pinned CDN, so it needs internet for that one dependency. The run starts by itself on load in Director mode.

**What was built**

- Ramp: a 42.6 m running surface sampled every 8 cm — flat approach, clothoid curvature blend into R≈13 m, lip at 115° and 18.6 m high (19.4 m at the truss top). The same samples drive the mesh and the physics surface query, so what you see is exactly what the tires feel. Concrete texture with stains and a white centre line, glowing red LED tubes on both edges, and a lattice steel truss with towers, X-bracing and struts following the hook.
- Car: pearl-silver Roadster wedge (4.5 × 2.0 × 1.15 m), long dark canopy, dark sills, aero-disc wheels, full-width tail/front light bars, `RDSTR` plate, diffuser nozzles, two spinning floor fans on the underside, and 14 thruster nozzles (4 lift, 8 side in two heights, 2 rear), each with a thrust-scaled pale cyan cold-gas jet.
- Physics: a hand-written rigid-body engine at fixed 240 Hz (capped steps per frame) — mass/inertia tensor with gyroscopic term, raycast-style suspension per wheel, friction-ellipse tires, ground-effect fan downforce applied at the two floor fans, body-corner crash contacts. A flight controller reads state and sets only throttle, fan power and per-nozzle thrust (lift allocation for pitch/roll, side couples for torque without sideways shove, tilt-vector translation, rear jets to clear the ramp). Slow motion changes only the clock.
- Breakage: 13 parts (front, rear, cabin core, hood, both doors, both bumpers, glass canopy, 4 wheels) detach on impact impulse thresholds; glass shatters into 14 shards; debris collides with ground, ramp and each other.
- Viewing/UI: Director (default), Foot/Wide/Lip/Drone/Aerial presets matching frames 01/02/14/21/23, Chase, free Orbit; Pause/Play (Space), 0.1×–2× speeds persisting across replays, a 30 Hz recorded-timeline scrubber with Live resume, Replay, live telemetry (speed, pitch, height, fan kg, firing thrusters, parts intact), and a settings panel (mass, fan kgf, drive kN, thruster kN, gravity) where every value feeds the simulation.

**Verified in a headless browser (real runs of the shipped file)**

- Default: wait → climb → hold ~2 s inverted at 105° surface pitch → release → jet roll → hover → touchdown at the ramp foot (z≈0) → drive-out → done in 17.5 s, 0 parts broken; two runs bit-identical (determinism delta 0). Real-time autostart also confirmed untouched, reaching drive-out with 13/13 parts.
- Low downforce (650 kgf): falls off the vertical, ends inverted wreck, all 12 breakable parts detached. Thruster failure (0 kN): climbs and hangs, then falls belly-up, canopy shatters, hood/bumpers tear off. Too slow (8 kN): stalls at 80°, rolls back, stops intact. Sensitivity sweep: mass 1,500–2,600 kg, gravity 3.7–12, thrust 40 kN, fan ≥2,000 kgf all still complete; fan 1,500 stalls and aborts; thrust 15 kN (below weight) crashes.
